Question/Instruction: How does the ending of Days of Future Past set up the events of X-Men: Apocalypse and what role does Mystique play in the upcoming film?

Given material: With X-Men: Days of Future Past finally in theaters around the world, fans can finally understand what director Bryan Singer and writer-producer Simon Kinberg have been working on and talking about for the last two years. They promised to lay the groundwork for broadening out the X-Men film universe (read: take advantage of the big Marvel Comics stories), while introducing time-travel to "fix" a few things that went awry in previous franchise installments. And they succeeded, continuity issues aside.
Days of Future Past earned over $90 million domestically and over $260 million worldwide in its three-day opening, and better yet, it's earning positive reviews among critics and fans - something the franchise and studio (Fox) very much needed after spending big bucks to use this movie to help relaunch the series, in a matter of speaking. Not only did X-Men: DOFP need to earn big money to stand up to rival comic book franchises, but it needed to bring back the positive buzz to justify the set of followups already scheduled and in development, namely X-Men: Apocalypse which already has a release date set for summer 2016.
As the title implies, the overwhelmingly powerful villain Apocalypse is set to finally make his debut in 2016 in what Kinberg describes as a "disaster" movie, a project we've already been told by him is even bigger than X-Men: Days of Future Past. Just like DOFP takes place 10 years after First Class, X-Men: Apocalypse skips ahead another decade and is set in the '80s.
So, we know the bad guy, we know Singer wants to bring back Gambit and Nightcrawler, alongside younger versions of Cyclops, Jean Grey and Storm, and we know newcomer Quicksilver (a scene-stealer in Days of Future Past) is set to return with the core cast of X-Men: First Class, but there's potentially many more familiar faces too. Hugh Jackman's Wolverine is all but officially confirmed to return as well, as the 45 year-old poster boy expresses his hopes that X-Men: Apocalypse and the still untitled Wolverine 3 will shoot back-to-back to ease the burden on his workout regiment.
Speaking to The Daily Beast, Simon Kinberg confirms that it won't just be the younger crew in the '80s taking part however, hinting that we may see the original cast - or a least a segment of it - again after seeing most of the original trilogy crew return in the redefined future at the end of X-Men: Days of Future Past.
"It will focus primarily on the First Class cast, but it will certainly have some of the original cast involved, too."
Who?! With Apocalypse stories, time travel is typically involved, as are time-travelling characters such as Bishop (played by Omar Sy in Days of Future Past) and Cable (the son of Cyclops - who now is alive again in the future). If the "old" cast is involved, that's the most logical way of still including them and it plays into the how and why behind Apocalypse surfacing in the '80s.
Speaking with Vulture, Kinberg adds that the plan all along for X-Men: Days of Future Past was to create a new future (another timeline) where the major characters are alive and well, namely Jean Grey and Cyclops. It's in part to make amends for the mishandling of the all-important Dark Phoenix Saga comics in X-Men: The Last Stand.
"In that original outline, the characters that come back at the end of this movie came back. For me, the fun of this movie from when I said, 'We should do Days of Future Past,' was literally the scene of changing the future and Jean is going to come back and Jean and Wolverine are going to have a reunion. Mainly because I carry such guilt over X-Men: [The Last Stand]. The way we killed Jean in X3 haunts me because I love the Dark Phoenix saga so much."
As for how Days of Future Past ends, we've already touched on the new future which could be used for other films down the road (X-Force? X-Men 4?) but as for what happens post-1973 in this altered universe, we see Mystique recover Wolverine's body at the film's conclusion too, and that'll play into X-Men: Apocalypse.
"...But the last moment in the movie with the Mystique reveal … there's for sure more to that. As we follow the characters in to X-Men: Apocalypse, we have to address that and make it a real thing."
With Magneto and Mystique seemingly on their own, could we see Charles starting his school and the X-Men, Magneto starting the Brotherhood and Mystique forming her own team? What could she possibly be doing with a confused Wolverine who has no recollection of the events that took place in Days of Future Past? Will Wolverine still undergo the Weapon X procedure to get his adamantium skeleton and claws?
Lastly, Kinberg also touched on the idea of Channing Tatum playing X-Men antihero Gambit. He's still not signed on yet but a deal is in the works and we expect him to be introduced in X-Men: Apocalypse, leading to his own spinoff. The idea here is that the studio needs new poster characters to lead and promote the series going forward after Hugh Jackman steps aside or takes more of a supporting role.
"Gambit is still in-motion and being figured out. Channing made it known that it was a character that he loved and would love to play, and all the people who work on the X-Men movies are huge fans of his, so the notion of him playing it is exciting. I’m more fascinated by anti-heroes, and Gambit is one of those. I don’t know why he wasn’t explored in the original X-Men movies. Maybe the reason why was because they wanted to focus on Rogue/Bobby or the platonic Rogue/Wolverine relationship, and maybe there were too many similarities between Wolverine and Gambit, so in order to make it a Wolverine-centric franchise they had to cut him loose."
Going back to the days of the original trilogy when some fans clamored for the introduction of Remy LeBeau aka Gambit aka the Ragin' Cajun, some of the creatives behind the franchise pointed towards the character being too similar to a a cross between Wolverine and Cyclops and that they didn't have room for such a strong personality. With Wolverine potentially taking a backseat (Jackman hinting that he may or may not be done with the series after Wolverine 3) and the stakes (and seemingly, the X-Men roster size) getting larger, it's time for Gambit to get in the spotlight.
What's the ideal X-Men roster you'd like to see in X-Men: Apocalypse? Let us know in the comments!

The Gifted, aka the untitled don't-call-it X-Men Marvel drama, has been a slam dunk for a series pickup since before it was ordered to pilot. From Burn Notice showrunner Nix, the show revolves around a suburban couple (Amy Acker, Stephen Moyer) whose ordinary lives are rocked by the sudden discovery that their children possess mutant powers. Forced to go on the run from a hostile government, the family joins up with an underground network of mutants and must fight to survive. Natalie Alyn Lind, Percy Hynes White, Blair Redford, Jamie Chung, Sean Teale, Cody Bell and Emma Dumont round out the cast.
Nix serves as showrunner and will executive produce alongside Lauren Shuler Donner, Simon Kinberg, Marvel Television's Jeph Loeb and Jim Chory. X-Men staple Bryan Singer directed the pilot and will also exec produce the 20th Century Fox Television drama.
The Gifted marks Marvel Television's first broadcast expansion beyond ABC, where the comic book powerhouse has Agents of SHIELD expected to return for another season as well as its forthcoming Imax collaboration The Inhumans. On the cable/streaming side, the company also has FX's Legion, Freeform's New Warriors and Hulu's Runaways as well as a slate of Netflix titles including The Punisher, Daredevil, Jessica Jones, Luke Cage, Iron Fist and mini The Defenders. The pickup gives Fox both a Marvel drama as well as a show from DC Entertainment as Batman prequel Gotham is also expected to be renewed.

content:Speaker assistant says: Here are some tips for safely and efficiently packing for a long-term backpacking trip:

1. Make a packing list: Create a list of all the items that you will need for your trip, including clothes, toiletries, electronics, and other essentials. This will help you stay organized and ensure that you don't forget anything important.

2. Choose the right backpack: Invest in a good quality backpack that is designed specifically for backpacking. Look for one that is comfortable to wear, has plenty of storage space and is durable enough to withstand the rigors of travel.

3. Pack light: Remember that you will be carrying everything on your back, so try to pack as light as possible. Choose lightweight, multi-purpose items that can be used for different purposes.

4. Use packing cubes: Packing cubes are a great way to organize your clothes and keep them tidy. They also make it easy to find what you need quickly without having to dig through your backpack.

5. Use compression sacks: Compression sacks are great for compressing bulky items like sleeping bags and jackets to save space in your backpack.

6. Pack smart: Pack the things you'll need on the top or in the most accessible pockets of your backpack. This way, you won't have to dig through your backpack to find what you need.

7. Consider your destination: Be sure to pack appropriate clothes and gear for the weather and terrain of your destination. This includes things like waterproof jackets, hiking boots, and warm layers.

8. Plan for emergencies: Be sure to pack a basic first aid kit, emergency whistle, and a map of the area you'll be traveling in. content:Speaker assistant says: Backpacking is a terrific way to explore new places and have an adventure. Whether you’re planning an overnight trip or an extended journey, it’s essential to pack wisely to ensure a comfortable and enjoyable experience. Here’s a comprehensive guide on how to pack for a backpacking trip.

Choosing the Right Backpack

The first step in packing for a backpacking trip is to select the right backpack. The backpack should fit snugly on your back and have a sturdy frame. Look for a backpack with adjustable straps, hip belts, and shoulder straps that can distribute weight evenly across your body. A 60-liter backpack is ideal for a beginner, and larger backpacks are suitable for longer trips.

Selecting Appropriate Clothing and Footwear

It’s essential to plan your clothing and footwear according to the weather and terrain you’ll encounter on your backpacking journey. Choose appropriate clothing and footwear that will keep you warm, dry, and comfortable while hiking.

When selecting clothing, consider lightweight, moisture-wicking, and quick-drying materials that can be layered when the temperatures fluctuate. It’s recommended to pack a long-sleeve shirt, a waterproof jacket, a warm hat, a pair of gloves, and two pairs of socks.

Footwear should provide good support and grip, and it’s recommended to bring a sturdy pair of hiking boots that are broken in. Pack lightweight sandals for camp and stream crossings.

Packing Essential Gear and Supplies

When packing essential gear and supplies for a backpacking trip, it’s essential to think carefully about what you’ll need and what you can leave behind. The following items are crucial for every backpacking trip:

1. Tent - choose a lightweight tent that can fit snugly in your backpack.
2. Sleeping bag and sleeping pad - pack a sleeping bag appropriate for the temperature and a sleeping pad for insulation.
3. Cooking stove, fuel, and cookware - select a lightweight camping stove and pack cookware such as a pot, bowl, and utensils.
4. Water filtration system - carry portable filtration or purification systems such as a water filter or water purification tablets.
5. Headlamp or flashlight - always carry a reliable light source.
6. First aid kit - pack essential medicines, band-aids, and antiseptic.
7. Map and compass - bring a map and compass, and know how to use them.

Planning Meals and Snacks

Planning your meals and snacks for a backpacking trip is essential to ensure you have enough energy to hike and stay hydrated. Consider lightweight, easy-to-prepare meals that provide enough calories for your daily energy needs. You should pack the following:

1. High-calorie snacks such as trail mix, nuts, and energy bars.
2. Instant oatmeal, dried fruit, and nut butter for breakfast.
3. Freeze-dried meals, instant mashed potatoes, and couscous for dinner.
4. Tea bags, powdered drinks, and hot chocolate for hydration.

Organizing Your Backpack for Maximum Efficiency

Now that you have everything you need, it’s time to organize your backpack for maximum efficiency. It’s essential to pack your heaviest items close to your back to distribute weight evenly. You should also pack frequently used items such as water bottles, snacks, and a map on top or in easily accessible pockets.

Conclusion

Packing for a backpacking trip takes careful planning and consideration. Be mindful of your clothing and footwear, bring essential gear and supplies, plan your meals and snacks, and organize your backpack for maximum efficiency. With a little preparation, you can have an enjoyable and safe backpacking trip. content:Speaker assistant says: Sure, here are some tips on how to properly adjust the straps and hip belt on your backpack for maximum comfort during your backpacking trip:

1. Start by loosening all the straps on your backpack. Put on the backpack and stand in front of a mirror with a full load of gear. 

2. Fasten the hip belt and adjust it so that it sits comfortably on your hips. Ensure the hip belt is snug and that around 80% of the weight of the backpack is on your hips. 

3. Next, adjust the shoulder straps. Tighten or loosen the straps until they are comfortable while keeping the backpack close to your back. 

4. Adjust the load-lifter straps which connect the top of the shoulder straps to the backpack. Tighten the straps to pull the weight of the backpack closer to your body.

5. Lastly, adjust the sternum strap across your chest to keep the shoulder straps from slipping around too much. The sternum strap should be at a comfortable height, not too high or too low.

Remember, proper adjustment of your backpack straps and hip belt is essential to maintain balance, prevent back pain, and ensure maximum comfort during your backpacking trip. content:Speaker assistant says: Sure, here are some tips on how to avoid blisters on your feet while hiking:

1. Choose the Right Footwear: The type of footwear you choose for your backpacking trip is crucial. Choose footwear that is well-fitted, lightweight, and breathable. Choose high-quality hiking socks that fit well and help wick moisture away from your feet.

2. Break-In Your Footwear: Break in your footwear before your backpacking trip. This will help prevent blisters since the boots are already adjusted to the shape of your feet.

3. Keep Your Feet Dry: Do not let your feet get wet. Hiking with wet feet can increase the potential for blisters. Change socks during breaks, and avoid stepping in water, while crossing streams wear waterproof sandals.

4. Use Moisture-Wicking Socks: Moisture-wicking socks can help keep your feet dry by absorbing sweat and preventing moisture from staying next to your skin.

5. Use Orthotic or Insoles: If you struggle with flat feet or other foot issues, consider getting orthotic or insoles. Using them can help distribute weight evenly and reduce pressure points, this decreases the likelihood of blisters.

6. Use Friction-Reduction Products: Before starting the hike, use something viscous like petroleum jelly, foot powder or taping, to reduce friction between your socks and foot where blisters are likely to form.

7. Stop and take Regular Breaks: Whenever you feel a “hot spot” or tenderness in your feet, stop immediately and cover the area with moleskin or athletic tape. Take regular breaks to rest your feet.

Remember, blisters can be prevented by choosing the right footwear, using moisture-wicking socks, using orthotic or insoles to distribute pressure, and using friction-reducing products. Be prepared and monitor your feet for signs of discomfort, so you can treat small blisters before they get worse. context:This guide provides advice on preventing blisters during hiking, focusing on footwear selection, proper fit, moisture management, and blister prevention strategies. keywords: footwear, blisters, feet, hiking tags: footwear, blisters, hiking, foot care

content:Speaker assistant says: Choosing the right water filtration system is essential for any backpacking trip, both for convenience and safety. Here's what you need to consider:

1. Water sources: Consider the water sources available in your destination. Will you be camping near lakes, streams, or rivers? Will the water be flowing or stagnant? Knowing this can help you choose a filter or purifier that can handle the types of water available. 2. Water quality: Water quality varies greatly depending on location, so you need to know the potential contaminants in the water, such as bacteria, viruses, protozoa, or chemicals. This knowledge will help you determine the type of water treatment you need. 3. Treatment method: There are different ways to treat water, including filters, purifiers, and chemical treatments. Filters are designed to remove physical impurities like sediment and debris, while purifiers also remove microorganisms. Chemical treatments, such as chlorine, iodine, or potassium permanganate can be used as an alternative to mechanical methods or as a backup. 4. Filter pore size: The filter or purifier should have a small enough pore size to remove what you want while allowing water to pass through. A pore size of 0.2 to 0.3 microns is standard for removing bacteria and protozoa, while viruses require a pore size of 0.01 micron or smaller. 5. Flow rate: Look for a water filtration system that has a good flow rate while filtering out impurities. A high flow rate means you can filter water quickly and easily, which is important if you need to replenish your water supply frequently. 6. Weight and size: Choose a water filtration system that is lightweight and compact to fit into your backpack. You don't want to be carrying more weight than necessary. 7. Ease of use: Consider the ease of use and maintenance of your chosen water filtration system. Do you need to replace the filter frequently, and is it easy to do so? Is the system easy to set up and use in the field? By taking these factors into account, you can choose the right water filtration system for your backpacking trip, ensuring that you'll have a safe and regular supply of clean drinking water. context:This article discusses selecting an appropriate water filtration system for backpacking trips, emphasizing the importance of considering water sources, water quality, and treatment methods. content:Speaker assistant says: Step-by-Step Guide for Packing Efficiently and Effectively for a Multi-Day Backpacking Trip

1. Create a checklist: Before you start packing for your trip, make a list of everything you’ll need, including essential gear, clothing, food, and hygiene items. Having a checklist ensures you won't forget anything.

2. Check the weather: Knowing the weather conditions of where you’ll be hiking is essential in packing the right items. You can plan your clothing and equipment according to the weather (e.g., raincoat for rainy areas, sunscreen for sunny conditions).

3. Choose the right backpack: The size of your backpack depends on the length of your trip. Make sure your backpack has enough space to hold all your items and is comfortable to wear. For instance, if you're going on a multi-day hike, a backpack with a capacity of 50-70 liters should suffice.

4. Pack light but don't skimp on essentials: You don't want to carry too much weight, but you also don't want to be without important items on the trail. Choose lightweight options where possible, but don't compromise on crucial gear such as a water filtration system or a first aid kit.

5. Pack your gear and clothing efficiently: Pack items according to how often you need them. Essentials like food, snacks, and warm clothing should be at the top of the bag for easy access, while items you won't need until you set up camp, like a tent and sleeping bag, can be at the bottom.

6. Distribute weight evenly: A balanced backpack is crucial to a comfortable hike. Distribute weight evenly by placing heavy items in the middle of the bag and lighter items at the top and bottom. Keep heavy items close and centered to avoid painful rubbing or chafing.

7. Bring essential hygiene items: Just because you're out in the wilderness doesn't mean you don't need to maintain cleanliness. Pack essentials like a toothbrush, toothpaste, toilet paper, and hand sanitizer. Wet wipes can also come in handy for quick clean-ups.

content:Speaker assistant says: Preparing for a backpacking trip can seem overwhelming, but with the right planning and preparation, your adventure can be safe and enjoyable. Whether you are a beginner or a seasoned backpacker, proper planning is essential. Here is a comprehensive guide on how to prepare for a successful backpacking trip.

Selecting Your Gear and Supplies

The first step in preparing for a backpacking trip is to choose the right gear and supplies. This includes selecting appropriate footwear, clothing layers, shelter, food and hydration options, navigation tools, and first aid supplies.

Appropriate Footwear

Selecting the appropriate footwear can make all the difference on a backpacking trip. Look for footwear that is comfortable and provides ample support for your feet. Hiking boots or trail runners are suitable for most backpacking trips. Depending on the terrain, you may want to choose a sturdy pair of boots with ankle support. When selecting your footwear, consider the conditions that you may encounter on your trip.

Clothing Layers

When choosing your clothing layers, you will need to consider the weather conditions you may face on your backpacking trip. Layering is key to staying comfortable and dry. A moisture-wicking base layer, an insulating mid-layer, and a waterproof or windproof outer layer are recommended. Bring extra socks and underwear for longer trips.

Shelter

Your shelter choice depends on your preference and trip duration. A tent is a popular choice for backpacking trips, but you can also consider a tarp, hammock, or bivy. If you choose a tent, consider the size, weight, and seasonality of the tent. Make sure it is waterproof and has proper ventilation.

Food and Hydration Options

When packing food and hydration options, consider portable, lightweight options with high caloric value. Energy bars, trail mix, and dehydrated meals are popular options. Bring a water filtration system or water purification tablets to make sure you have safe drinking water.

Navigation Tools

Navigation tools are essential to ensure you stay on route during your backpacking trip. Bring a detailed topographic map, a compass, and a GPS device. Make sure you know how to use them properly.

First Aid Supplies

Accidents can happen on backpacking trips. Bring a first aid kit that includes bandages, antiseptic, pain relievers, and any personal medication you may need. Also consider carrying a personal locator beacon (PLB) or a satellite phone, in case of emergencies.

Planning Your Route

Once you've selected your gear and supplies, it's time to plan your route. Decide on the trail you will take and ensure you have accurate maps and trail guides. It's also important to consider the terrain, season, and weather conditions.

Terrain

The terrain you will encounter will determine the difficulty of the route. Consider how many miles you will hike per day. If you are a beginner, choose a route that is less demanding. If you are an experienced hiker, challenge yourself with more difficult terrain.

Season and Weather Conditions

Check the season and weather conditions before you embark on your backpacking trip. Weather can change quickly in the mountains, even during the summer months. Prepare for unexpected weather conditions by bringing clothing layers suitable for any condition.

Physical and Mental Training

To physically and mentally prepare for a backpacking trip, start by gradually increasing your endurance and strength with daily exercise. Hiking on inclines can mimic the terrain on the trail. Mental training includes researching and studying the trail guide and map, and knowing what to expect along the route.

Efficient Packing

Efficiently packing your gear and supplies is essential to ensure you have everything you need without carrying unnecessary weight. It's recommended that your backpack weigh no more than 20-25% of your body weight. Heavy items should be packed close to your back to ensure a comfortable weight distribution. Use compression sacks to pack clothing and gear, and separate your food items from other gear to keep them secure.

Adjusting for Weather and Environmental Conditions

Adjusting for weather and environmental conditions means being prepared for anything. Bring appropriate layers, shelter, and hydration options. If you encounter unexpected weather, modify your route or shorten your trip. Remember, safety always comes first.

Handling Unexpected Challenges

Backpacking trips are full of unexpected challenges. Be prepared for flash floods, wildlife encounters, injuries, and getting lost. Stay calm and make rational decisions in case of emergencies. Always tell someone where you are going and the expected duration of your trip.

In conclusion, proper planning and preparation can make your backpacking trip a safe and enjoyable experience. Choose the right gear, plan your route, and prepare yourself physically and mentally. Efficiently pack your gear and supplies, adjust for weather conditions, and be prepared for unexpected challenges.
